name: dev_v4
scoring: Labels are intersected with the topics eligible for the trial state. If 'expected' has no eligible topic, 'fallback_expected' is used. exact: selection equals expected. acceptable: every ID is in 'acceptable' and at least one is in 'required' (when any required topic is eligible). partial: hits 'required' but includes an ID outside 'acceptable'. incorrect: misses 'required'.

questions.question: has my result come through yet?
questions.why: The plan's answer above already states the result. With no result yet, 'why there's no conclusion' is the focused explanation; once a result exists that topic is ineligible and the next step is the useful addition.

questions.question: I can't find my verdict anywhere
questions.why: The plan's answer above already states the result. With no result yet, 'why there's no conclusion' is the focused explanation; once a result exists that topic is ineligible and the next step is the useful addition.

questions.question: does a phone-photo test tell you anything real about skin?
questions.why: Limits says what a result can show; the band says how much photo variation there is. Photo comparability is a fair extra.

questions.question: be straight with me, is this a proper test or just for show?
questions.why: Limits is the direct answer; band, fixed date and photo rules all describe how the test is set up.

questions.question: if the numbers went the wrong way would it say so?
questions.why: Detectability says in advance whether a drop can register; limits says a result reports movement beyond the band.

questions.question: do bad results get hidden?
questions.why: As d05. No text promises anything beyond these.

questions.question: the scores are consistent, so the cream must be good, right?
questions.why: Limits separates a measured change from what caused it; band is a fair extra about consistency.

questions.question: being repeatable and the product working aren't the same thing, are they?
questions.why: Both halves of the question: band (repeatability) and limits (not efficacy).

questions.question: if I snap two selfies back to back, will they score the same?
questions.why: The band is exactly this variation; the instrument check is the product's way to measure it.

questions.question: what's the second baseline photo actually for?
questions.why: Instrument check is the direct answer.

questions.question: why not make the band tighter so it catches smaller changes?
questions.why: Band explains why a change inside it can't count. Instrument check is not acceptable: it only widens.

questions.question: is the band the same thing as the instrument check?
questions.why: Both topics are named.

questions.question: so?
questions.why: Too vague: the safe fixed answer is preferred to a guessed topic.

questions.question: go on then
questions.why: As d13.

questions.question: hmm ok but
questions.why: As d13.

questions.question: promise me this cream will fix my dry patches
questions.why: A promise and a skin complaint: out of scope; limits (no predictions, not medical advice) is a fair alternative.

questions.question: would switching to a retinol speed things up?
questions.why: Product switching: the plan's next step plus limits, or the out-of-scope text.

questions.question: my skin is peeling a bit, carry on?
questions.why: A symptom and a usage decision: out of scope only.

questions.question: was the jump down to the new cream?
questions.why: Causal: limits says it can't show why.

questions.question: guarantee me it keeps working next month
questions.why: Guarantee/prediction: limits or out of scope.
